gaps.sentence: The recipe ___ (pass down) from generation to generation.
gaps.hint: continuing relevance from past to now
gaps.explanation: Present perfect passive: has been + passed down; the process links past and present.

gaps.sentence: I must get my passport ___ (renew) before the trip.
gaps.explanation: 'Get + object + past participle': the passport is renewed by an authority, not by me.

gaps.sentence: The match ___ (abandon) because of the storm, so we got a refund.
gaps.explanation: Modal passive with have to: had to be + past participle for past obligation.

gaps.sentence: There's still a lot of paperwork ___ (complete) before we can close the account.
gaps.explanation: Noun + passive to-infinitive (paperwork to be completed) — the paperwork receives the action.

gaps.sentence: The museum ___ (close) to the public on Mondays.
gaps.explanation: Present simple passive: is + closed. No agent needed; the routine is what matters.

gaps.sentence: Endangered plants ___ (not pick) anywhere in the reserve.
gaps.explanation: Modal passive of prohibition: must not be + past participle.

gaps.sentence: She ___ (think) to be the finest violinist of her generation.
gaps.explanation: Impersonal passive: is thought to be. The thinkers are general, not stated.

gaps.sentence: The temple is thought ___ (build) more than two thousand years ago.
gaps.explanation: Perfect passive infinitive: to have been + built for an event earlier than the main verb.
